resources.string: Phone role, permissions, data regions and battery settings
A phone app that keeps everything on your device. It names businesses and warns you about unwanted calls using lists stored on your phone.
Phone numbers never leave your device.
No account and no internet connection are needed.
Every step after this one is optional and can be done later in Settings.
Android lets you choose which app handles calls and which one screens them. Both choices are optional and you can change them at any time in Android settings.
Shows incoming calls, the call screen and your call history.
Lets the app check an incoming number against your lists before the phone rings.
Each permission is requested on its own, with the reason. You can refuse any of them; the matching feature simply stays off.
Android is not asking again. You can allow it in the app\'s system settings.
Needed to place calls, to know which SIM is used and to answer or reject calls from the call screen.
Needed to show names for numbers, to search while you dial and to edit your contacts. Contacts are never uploaded.
Needed to show and manage your recent calls.
Needed to show incoming and missed calls when the app is not on screen.
Choose the countries whose business names and prefix rules you want. They are signed packs downloaded to your phone, and you can remove them at any time.
The list of regions could not be loaded. You can retry, or skip this step and choose in Settings > Data when you are online.
You seem to be offline. Showing the last list that was downloaded.
Nothing selected. You can add regions later in Settings > Data.
You are not on Wi-Fi. Downloads wait for Wi-Fi unless you change that in Settings > Data.
You will be able to sync your own spam list and allowlist with your Nextcloud. This is optional and arrives in a later update.
Some phones stop background apps to save battery, which can delay the call screen or hide it over the lock screen. These settings prevent that.
This phone has no screen for that. Follow the steps above in Android settings.
Full-screen calls over the lock screen
This is where things stand. You can change any of it later.
The download starts as soon as you finish.
There is no suitable connection now. The download starts automatically when you are on Wi-Fi.
Open Settings > Battery and find UltimatePhone in the app list. Allow background activity and do not let the system optimise or restrict it.
Open Settings > Apps > Auto-start (or App management > Auto-launch) and switch UltimatePhone on.
Open Settings > Apps > App management > UltimatePhone > Permissions and allow “Display pop-ups while running in the background” and “Display over other apps”.
In the same permissions page allow full-screen notifications or lock screen display, so the call screen can appear when the phone is locked.
Open Settings > Battery > Background usage limits. Remove UltimatePhone from “Sleeping apps” and “Deep sleeping apps” and add it to “Never sleeping apps”.
Samsung has no separate auto-start list. Just make sure UltimatePhone is not in “Sleeping apps” or “Deep sleeping apps”.
Open Settings > Apps > UltimatePhone > Appear on top and switch it on.
Allow full-screen notifications for UltimatePhone (Settings > Notifications > Advanced settings, or the app\'s notification settings).
Open Settings > Apps > Manage apps > UltimatePhone > Battery saver and choose “No restrictions”.
Open Security > Permissions > Autostart and switch UltimatePhone on.
Open the app\'s Other permissions and allow “Display pop-up windows while running in the background”.
In the same Other permissions page, allow “Show on lock screen”.
Allow UltimatePhone to ignore battery optimisation: show “All apps”, find UltimatePhone and choose “Don\'t optimise”.
Not needed on this phone: Android does not restrict auto-start.
Usually not needed. Open the app info if call screens ever fail to appear.
Allow full-screen notifications for UltimatePhone so incoming calls can appear over the lock screen (Android 14 and later).
Look for battery or power settings, find UltimatePhone and exclude it from battery optimisation and background restrictions.
If your phone has an auto-start or auto-launch list (often under Security or Apps), switch UltimatePhone on.
If your phone has a pop-up or display-over-other-apps permission, allow it for UltimatePhone.
Allow UltimatePhone to show full-screen notifications or to display over the lock screen, so incoming calls appear when the phone is locked.
